correctness.rationale: Writing H=e^{-(x²+y²)}(cosh(2ax)+cos(2ay))/2 yields xD=a sinh(2ax), yD=-a sin(2ay). If xy≠0, sinh(2ax)/(2ax)>1 while -sin(2ay)/(2ay)≤1: impossible. Imaginary roots y=-a tan(ay) are uniquely isolated by strict monotonicity on the stated half-periods, with Hessian signs (+,-); simple cosh zeros have Hessian 2a² exp(-|z₀|²)I. On real axis x=a tanh(ax) has positive solution only for a>1; the origin Hessian is (2(a²-1),-2(a²+1)), with -x⁴/6 at a=1. Global inequality H(x+iy)≤e^{-x²}cosh²(ax) proves the global maxima without a numerical scan. Independently differentiated the logarithm and checked the quartic series symbolically.
